Hi Alex — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery + a concrete set of next steps so we keep momentum. High-level notes below (kept short), then action items and owners.

Call summary
- Goal: Integratek wants an LLM-powered assistant embedded in your support console to (a) surface relevant KB articles via embeddings + rerankers, (b) run a small set of domain tools (ticket lookup, run a policy check, create an incident) using tool/function calling, and (c) meet your latency target (~250ms P95 for quick lookups).
- Constraints: Sensitive customer data must remain in-region (US), SSO and provisioning via Okta, and procurement prefers hosted + Private option evaluation for long-term residency.

Technical follow-ups from the call
1) SDK setup & auth: Recommend using Redwood SDK v1.4 for quick integration. Auth pattern: short-lived API keys minted by your backend (Okta-backed service account) — Redwood supports token introspection + KMS for keys. We can demo Okta OIDC flow + automated token rotation during the architecture review.
2) Routing & fallbacks: Use routing policy to prefer smaller, faster models for quick KB lookups and fall back to higher-capacity variants for complex completions. We’ll show cost/latency profiles so you can pick the sweet spot.
3) Structured output + tool calling: Strongly recommend tool definitions with strict input schemas and structured outputs (JSON schema). For critical ops (ticket lookup / incident create) we suggest synchronous tool calls with validation and a retry + idempotency key. For background enrichments (async audit run) use async tool calling with status endpoints.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: Use embeddings for candidate retrieval + a small neural reranker to boost precision. We'll recommend an embedding model and a fast in-memory vector store approach (approximate NN) for sub-50ms candidate retrieval to stay within your latency SLO.

- redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + code snippets)

- Priyom: create a demo repo showing tool definitions + sample reranker pipeline; will include a small dataset and guidance for sandboxing. (owner: priyom.das@redwood.ai)
- Olga: coordinate procurement intro and get any initial non-disclosure paperwork started. (owner: olga.petrov@redwood.ai)

- Are you comfortable with the short-lived API key pattern (Okta -> mint service token -> Redwood), or do you require an enterprise SSO-only flow from day one?

If that looks right I’ll book the architecture review once you confirm availability. Thanks again — good call.

Alex — quick technical notes that might answer the latency/cost question and outline recommended tool-calling patterns. Short bullets, then a small example of a tool definition and error handling pattern.

Latency/cost tradeoffs
- Embedding model: use a mid-size embedding model (fewer tokens, cheaper) for candidate retrieval, then rerank with a small cross-encoder model only on top-N (N=8-16) candidates. This keeps token costs low and CPU/GPU work bounded.
- Caching: prefix + KV caching for repeated queries reduces generation tokens. For KB lookups cache embedding vectors and the reranker inputs where possible.

Tool/function calling patterns (recommended)
- Define tools with explicit schemas: id, name, inputSchema (JSON Schema), outputSchema, timeoutMs, idempotencyKeyBehaviour.
- Synchronous critical tools: ticket_lookup, create_incident — call, validate response, return structured output to the model so downstream UI can render.
- Parallel vs sequential: for independent enrichment tasks (metadata fetch, spam-check, policy-check) dispatch parallel worker tools and aggregate results. For dependent tasks (ticket lookup -> incident create) run sequentially and persist state with idempotency to avoid duplicate creates.
- Error handling: model-facing errors should be normalized. Example: if a tool times out, return {"tool_error":"timeout","retryable":true,"details":"timeout after 12000ms"} and your orchestration should either retry with backoff or escalate to a fallback tool.

Mini example (pseudo-schema)
{
  "tool_id": "ticket_lookup_v1",
  "name": "Ticket Lookup",
  "inputSchema": {"type":"object","properties":{"ticket_id":{"type":"string"}}},
  "outputSchema": {"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"assignee":{"type":"string"}}},
  "timeoutMs": 12000
}

We’ll include concrete SDK snippets in the demo repo showing how the Redwood SDK performs tool calls and surface structured outputs to the UI. On the Private/hosted question: you can start with hosted dedicated tenancy for the POC if your compliance team accepts contractual data controls; Private is recommended if you need full VPC/on-prem isolation. Happy to walk through the exact controls during the arch review.
